Samir —

Really appreciate the clear ask. Per our call and your checklist, I put together a concise POC playbook (attached) and a proposed timeline below. High level: 2-week focused trial that validates (1) integration stability (SDK + API + streaming), (2) latency/cost at your average request sizes, and (3) quality on your prompt set for the top 3 user journeys.

Proposed success criteria (suggested, happy to adjust):
- Functional: SDK integration in sandbox + sample flow exercising streaming and function/tool-calling (end-to-end request->response)
- Performance: median token latency <= 210ms for 512-token context under 50 rps sustained (defined test harness)
- Cost: per-token unit cost estimate within 20% of target (we'll provide run report)
- Quality: >= 92% pass rate on your 50-item prompt set for critical intents (we will collaborate on evals)

POC timeline (target):
- Day 0 (kickoff): alignment + access provisioning
- Day 1–3: network allowlist + sample SDK integration
- Day 4–8: run synthetic load + streaming validation; iterate on prompts
- Day 9–12: run customer prompt evals, gather metrics
- Day 13–14: demo results, handoff/next steps (dedicated or hosted plan)

Ownership:
- Redwood commercial: Sergio Alvarez (project owner — project coordination & deliverables)
- Redwood technical: Marcus Lin (SE — SDK, API, streaming, infra)
- NovaRetail technical: Samir (owner) and Priya (POC PM)

I've attached a draft playbook (poc-playbook-v1.xlsx) with an ops checklist, test harness steps, and a minimal SOW checklist you can pass to procurement. If that looks good I can schedule a 30min technical kickoff Wed 2026-06-23 10:00am PT — Marcus can run the demo of the SDK + sample flows.

Hi Samir / team —

Quick technical follow-up and what I'll bring to the kickoff. Key integration notes: 

1) SDKs & sample flows
- We support JS/TS and Python SDKs; sample repo includes streaming examples and a small server-side proxy for token handling. We'll share api-samples.zip in the Drive link (small zip with sample app).

2) API routes & streaming
- Typical call patterns: POST /v1/generate (sync), POST /v1/stream for SSE/websocket streaming, and POST /v1/call for function/tool calling workflows. Auth: Bearer API key, optional mTLS for Private deployments.
- For streaming we suggest using the SSE endpoint for browser prototypes; the SDK wraps reconnect and partial tokens.

3) Tool calling (function calls)
- We support structured function schemas; best practice is to register functions with return-type schemas and use the /v1/call endpoint. Marcus will provide a short example on kickoff.

4) Network & infra
- Outbound egress: allow 52.14.23.0/24 and 34.210.45.0/24 (sample IPs; final list in network_requirements.pdf). Ports: 443 TLS.
- If you want locked-down VPC peering or Private deployment options, we can scope that — but for the trial the IP allowlist + API key is fastest.

5) Data handling & logs
- By default logs are redacted; we can enable token-level tracing for debugging for the POC period and share a secure link to results.

Small snippet (pseudo-Python) to get you started:

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
# streaming example
for chunk in client.stream_generate(model="redwood-lite-v1", prompt=prompt):
    print(chunk.text, end="")

I'll bring the sample app and a short checklist to the kickoff. If you can grant Marcus access to a small sandbox account (email to follow) we'll pre-seed the test prompts.

Regards,
Marcus Lin

marcus@redwood.ai
